[[Category:Matrix operation]]
[[Category:Vector operation]]
'''Hadamard-Schur product''' ('''element-wise product''') generalises component-wise multiplication to [[vector]]s and [[matrix|matrices]].

== Definition ==

=== Matrices ===

For matrices $\mathbf{A}=(a_{ij}), \mathbf{B}=(b_{ij}) \in \mathbb{F}^{m \times n}$

$$
(\mathbf{A} \circ \mathbf{B})_{ij} = a_{ij} b_{ij}.
$$

=== Vectors ===

For vectors $\vec u, \vec v \in \mathbb{F}^n$,

$$
(\vec u \circ \vec v)_i = u_i v_i.
$$

<blockquote>
Do not confuse the '''Hadamard-Schur product''' with [[vector dot product]], both multiple two vectors of same dimension component-wise, but the former returns a new vector of that dimension while the latter sums over the component-wise products and return a scalar.
</blockquote>

== Properties ==

The Hadamard-Schur product is '''commutative, associative, and distributive''':

$$
\begin{cases}
\mathbf{A} \circ \mathbf{B} = \mathbf{B} \circ \mathbf{A} \\
(\mathbf{A} \circ \mathbf{B}) \circ \mathbf{C} = \mathbf{A} \circ (\mathbf{B} \circ \mathbf{C}) \\
\mathbf{A} \circ (\mathbf{B} + \mathbf{C}) = \mathbf{A} \circ \mathbf{B} + \mathbf{A} \circ \mathbf{C}
\end{cases}
$$

== Identity element ==

The '''identity element''' for the Hadamard-Schur product on $\mathbb{F}^{m \times n}$ is

$$
\mathbf{J}_{m \times n}: \forall i \in \{1,\cdots,m\}, j \in \{1,\cdots,n\}: (\mathbf{J})_{ij} = 1
$$

which verifies

$$
\forall \mathbf{A}_{m \times n}: \mathbf{A} \circ \mathbf{J}_{m \times n} = \mathbf{A}.
$$
